approachQuestion.prompt: A binary image has r rows and c columns, with 1 ≤ r,c and r×c ≤ 200,000. Count all nonempty axis-aligned rectangular regions containing only 1s. Rectangles with different boundaries are distinct. Example: [[1,1],[1,1]] returns 9: four single cells, two horizontal pairs, two vertical pairs, and the full square. Choose the best approach.
constraints: The immutable binary image has r rows and c columns, with 1 ≤ r,c and r×c ≤ 200,000. Counts and arithmetic results fit signed 64-bit words; access and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: Maintain consecutive-1 column heights for each row. Within a row keep increasing (height, count) groups and a running total S. For height h start count=1; pop groups with height at least h, subtracting height×count from S and merging their counts. Push (h,count), add h×count to S, and add S to the answer. Reset groups and S for each row.
options.feedback: For a fixed bottom row and right column, each left boundary contributes the minimum height over its column interval. S is the sum of those suffix minima; height groups compress suffixes with the same minimum, and each height unit corresponds to a distinct top row.

options.text: Sum every consecutive-1 column height over all rows and return that total.
options.feedback: This counts only width-one rectangles. For [[1,1]], it returns 2 instead of 3.

options.text: For every row compute the area of its largest histogram rectangle and sum these areas.
options.feedback: Areas do not count distinct boundary choices. For [[1,1]], the largest area is 2, but there are 3 all-1 rectangles.

options.text: Enumerate every rectangle’s four boundaries and inspect its cells, counting it if all are 1.
options.feedback: It counts correctly but repeatedly inspects a huge collection of overlapping rectangles. Suffix-height groups aggregate these choices without enumerating them.

feedback.reason: Maintain the sum of minima of all suffixes through compressed height groups while accumulating rectangle counts.
details: For each bottom row update column heights. Scan them with a stack of increasing height groups, tracking how many suffixes share each height. When a smaller or equal height arrives, replace affected groups and adjust the suffix-minimum sum. Add that sum for each right column.

For a fixed bottom row and right column, the sum of suffix minimum heights counts all rectangles ending there. Height groups compress equal minima across different starts; adding only the largest rectangle would miss smaller ones.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For height-suffix-totals, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n=r×c. Store c heights and a reused stack of at most c groups. The result is a scalar count. All counts and products fit signed 64-bit words.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(c) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Per-row group pushes/pops are linear and use column-sized state.
details: Each row processes c heights, and each group is pushed once and popped at most once. Across all rows time is O(r×c)=O(n). Heights and the reused group stack use O(c) auxiliary space.
